src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/TreeBuilder.java — holds CharacterReader, Tokeniser, Document doc, stack of open Elements, currentToken, TagSet, optional LineMap for position tracking. Drive loop:
- `initialiseParse()` sets doc, reader, tokeniser, tagSet, stack.
- `runParser()` loops `stepParser()` till false, then `completeParse()`.
- `stepParser()`: on EOF token pops stack elems one-by-one (hits onNodeClosed callbacks) till empty; else `tokeniser.read()` -> `currentToken` -> abstract `process(token)` -> `token.reset()`.
`process(Token)` is abstract — each subclass (Html/Xml) implements differently. Also holds hooks `tagFor(...)` (TagSet lookup), `enforceStackDepthLimit()`, `onNodeInserted/onNodeClosed` (source-range + listener callbacks), `defaultMaxDepth()` (512 base, XmlTreeBuilder overrides to MAX_VALUE).

- `defaultNamespace()`: Html inherits base `NamespaceHtml` (TreeBuilder.java); Xml overrides to `NamespaceXml` (XmlTreeBuilder.java).
- `defaultTagSet()`: Html base → `TagSet.Html()` full HTML5 tag defaults (block/inline/void/rcdata/data/formSubmittable/textBoundary bits, set up in `TagSet.initHtmlDefault()`, src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/TagSet.java); Xml → `new TagSet()` empty, so no tag preconceptions, all tags generic unless discovered.

## Parser subsystem overview

Top-level entry: `Parser` class holds a `TreeBuilder` (either `HtmlTreeBuilder` or `XmlTreeBuilder`), plus settings/errors/tagset. `Parser.parseInput` just locks and delegates to `treeBuilder.parse(...)` (Parser.java:88-95). Static factories `htmlParser()`/`xmlParser()` pick tree builder impl (Parser.java:369-380).

### TreeBuilder (base, abstract)
`TreeBuilder` (abstract) owns the shared plumbing: `CharacterReader reader`, `Tokeniser tokeniser`, `Document doc`, stack of open `Element`s, current token, settings, tagset (TreeBuilder.java:22-32). Init sets up reader/tokeniser/doc per parse (TreeBuilder.java:41-62). Main loop: `runParser()` calls `stepParser()` repeatedly until EOF is fully drained; each step pulls one `Token` from tokeniser (`tokeniser.read()`), stores as `currentToken`, and calls abstract `process(token)` (TreeBuilder.java:105-130). `process(Token)` is abstract — each concrete tree builder implements its own dispatch (TreeBuilder.java:130). Base class also provides shared stack ops (`push`/`pop`), depth-limit enforcement (`enforceStackDepthLimit`, TreeBuilder.java:182-189), default namespace (`NamespaceHtml`, TreeBuilder.java:273-275) and default tagset (`TagSet.Html()`, TreeBuilder.java:277-279), both overridden by XML side.

### Tokeniser (lexer / low-level state machine)
`Tokeniser` reads chars off `CharacterReader` and turns them into `Token`s, driven by a `TokeniserState state` field (Tokeniser.java:34-37). `read()` loops `state.read(this, reader)` until a token is emitted (Tokeniser.java:64-77). Knows `syntax` (html vs xml) captured at construction from whether tree builder is `XmlTreeBuilder` (Tokeniser.java:56). Produces token types: Doctype, StartTag, EndTag, Comment, Character, XmlDecl, EOF (Token.java:620-626).

`TokeniserState` is a big enum, one state per method `read(Tokeniser,CharacterReader)`, implementing HTML5 tokenizer states — Data, TagOpen, RCDATA/rawtext/scriptdata variants, attribute states, comment/doctype states, plus XML-specific `MarkupProcessingOpen` (PI) and `CdataSection` (TokeniserState.java:11-1677, listing ~60 states e.g. TokeniserState.java:12,100,151,927,940,965,1677). Transition to next state via `t.transition(...)`/`t.advanceTransition(...)` (Tokeniser.java:118-129). `TagOpen` state branches on `t.syntax == xml` to go to `MarkupProcessingOpen` for `<?`, else treats it as bogus comment for HTML (TokeniserState.java:110-116).

### Tree builder state machine (parser proper)
`HtmlTreeBuilder extends TreeBuilder` implements `process(Token)` by dispatching to a **second** state machine, `HtmlTreeBuilderState` — an enum of HTML5 "insertion modes" (Initial, BeforeHtml, BeforeHead, InHead, InBody, Text, InTable, ... AfterAfterFrameset, ForeignContent — ~23 states, HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:25-1746). Each state implements `process(Token t, HtmlTreeBuilder tb)` (abstract at HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:1853) mutating the open-element stack/doc and possibly calling `tb.transition(...)` to move to another insertion mode (example: `Initial` state builds doctype then `tb.transition(BeforeHtml)`, HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:25-50).

`HtmlTreeBuilder.process` first checks a "noscript island" special-case (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:152-154), then decides whether to use the current insertion-mode state or divert to the special `ForeignContent` state via `useCurrentOrForeignInsert(token)` (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:155-156). That helper implements the HTML5 "adjusted current node" foreign-content rules (MathML text integration points, HTML integration points, empty stack, EOF) per spec (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:233-270), and `ForeignContent` state itself implements the spec's in-foreign-content algorithm, occasionally falling back to `processAsHtml` (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:1746-1836).

There's a feedback loop between the two state machines: tree-builder states, on seeing tags like `title`, `script`, `style`, `textarea`, or custom raw/rcdata tags (via `Tag.textState()`, Tag.java:344), push the tokeniser into a different lexing mode (e.g. `ScriptData`, `Rawtext`) so raw markup content isn't tokenised as tags — done both when entering head (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:113-115), in `InHead`/`InBody` states (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:136-145,593-595), and even inside `ForeignContent` for e.g. embedded SVG `script` (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:1783-1789).

### XmlTreeBuilder — how it differs
`XmlTreeBuilder extends TreeBuilder` too, but its `process(Token)` is a single flat `switch` on token type — StartTag → `insertElementFor`, EndTag → `popStackToClose`, Comment/Character/Doctype/XmlDecl → direct leaf-node inserts (XmlTreeBuilder.java:114-144). There is **no** analogous "insertion-mode" enum for XML: no `HtmlTreeBuilderState`-style state machine, no auto-generated implicit elements, no foster-parenting/foreign-content algorithm, no formatting-element reconstruction — XML trusts the input structure directly.

Concrete structural differences baked into the two TreeBuilder subclasses:
- Default settings: HTML default settings vs XML `ParseSettings.preserveCase` (case-preserving) (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:58-60 vs XmlTreeBuilder.java:42-44).
- Default namespace: HTML → `NamespaceHtml` (inherited default, TreeBuilder.java:273-275); XML → `NamespaceXml`, overridden (XmlTreeBuilder.java:100-102).
- Default tag set: HTML → `TagSet.Html()` with known tag semantics (TreeBuilder.java:277-279); XML → an empty `TagSet`, i.e. no built-in tag knowledge unless user supplies one via `Parser.tagSet()` (XmlTreeBuilder.java:104-107; Parser.java:224-247).
- Max stack depth: HTML defaults to 512 (TreeBuilder.java:201-203); XML defaults to `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, effectively unlimited (XmlTreeBuilder.java:109-112, also set explicitly in `Parser.xmlParser()`, Parser.java:378-380).
- XML does its own namespace bookkeeping manually with a `namespacesStack` of prefix→URI maps, processing `xmlns`/`xmlns:` attrs on each element push/pop (XmlTreeBuilder.java:40,54-58,146-163,180-218), whereas HTML namespace assignment is baked into the fixed insertion-mode/foreign-content logic (namespaces `NamespaceHtml`/`NamespaceMathml`/`NamespaceSvg` constants defined centrally, Parser.java:22-25).
- Both tree builders still share the same `Tokeniser`/`TokeniserState` lexer, with syntax-sensitive branches (e.g. `<?` handling in `TagOpen`, TokeniserState.java:110-116) and both can redirect the tokeniser into text/rawtext/rcdata states based on `Tag.textState()` (HtmlTreeBuilder.java:113-115; XmlTreeBuilder.java:67-68,175-176) — so the lexer layer is essentially shared/reused, only the tree-construction layer diverges (two-level state machine for HTML vs flat switch for XML).

### Summary of roles
- **Tokeniser** = lexer: turns char stream into `Token`s, itself a state machine (`TokeniserState`) tracking things like tag-open, attribute, comment, doctype, script/rawtext escaping states (Tokeniser.java:14-77; TokeniserState.java:11-1677).
- **TreeBuilder** = shared driver/DOM-builder base: owns stack of open elements, feeds tokens from tokeniser into `process()`, manages document, error/position tracking (TreeBuilder.java:22-130).
- **Parser state machine** (`HtmlTreeBuilderState`) = HTML5 insertion-mode state machine layered on top of `HtmlTreeBuilder`, doing the real HTML5 tree-construction algorithm including foreign content (`ForeignContent`) handling; XML skips this layer entirely and just applies tokens directly to the stack (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:24-1853 vs XmlTreeBuilder.java:114-144).

Caller/HTTP-supplied charset, if present, simply wins — no comparison vs doc's declared meta charset happens at all.** Guard `if (charsetName == null)` `DataUtil.java:259` means: when charsetName is non-null (from `Jsoup.parse(..., charsetName)` param, or from HTTP `Content-Type` header parsed into `res.charset` at `HttpConnection.java:976` via `DataUtil.getCharsetFromContentType` `DataUtil.java:370`), the whole meta/xml-decl sniff block (lines 259-311) is skipped entirely. Doc's own declared `<meta charset>`/`http-equiv`/`<?xml encoding?>` never even inspected in that case. Only check left is non-empty validate `DataUtil.java:313`. So "conflict" isn't really resolved by comparison — supplied charset just overrides, meta ignored. Same pattern in `HttpConnection.parse()`: `charset` field set from header before parse `HttpConnection.java:976`, passed straight into `DataUtil.parseInputStream(stream, charset, ...)` `HttpConnection.java:1051`.

**3. Re-parse trigger only fires when NO charset was supplied by caller/HTTP** (charsetName null and no BOM). Then:
- Doc first speculatively parsed as UTF-8, capped to a small lookahead buffer `firstReadBufferSize = 1024*5` `DataUtil.java:50`, via marked/reset stream `DataUtil.java:259-273`.
- Speculative doc scanned for `<meta http-equiv=content-type>` / `<meta charset>` (evaluator `metaCharset` `DataUtil.java:238`, scan loop `DataUtil.java:276-285`) or `<?xml encoding=...?>` decl `DataUtil.java:288-301`.
- Found value validated via `validateCharset` (must be JVM-supported charset name) `DataUtil.java:381-392`.
- **Re-parse decision point:** if a valid found charset differs (case-insensitively) from default UTF-8, code sets `charsetName = foundCharset` and **`doc = null`** — `DataUtil.java:303-306`. That `doc = null` is the actual re-parse trigger: `parseInputStream(CharsetDoc, ...)` only reuses the speculative doc when `charsetDoc.doc != null` `DataUtil.java:325-326`; when null it builds a fresh `SimpleStreamReader` with the now-correct `Charset` and calls `parser.parseInput` again `DataUtil.java:328-338`.
- If found charset equals default UTF-8, speculative doc already correct: kept/reused for regular (non-stream) parse if input was fully consumed (`reuseDocIfFullyRead && input.baseReadFully()`) `DataUtil.java:307-309`; for the streaming-parser path (`reuseDocIfFullyRead=false`, set at `DataUtil.java:246-247`) it's nulled anyway so a real re-decodable reader gets built `DataUtil.java:310`.

**4. Post-parse charset bookkeeping.** After final parse, `doc.outputSettings().charset(charset)` sets output charset `DataUtil.java:339`; if that charset can't encode (some read-only charsets), doc is force-switched to UTF-8 via `doc.charset(UTF_8)` `DataUtil.java:340-342`, which updates the output charset and can rewrite the document's own `<meta charset>`/xml-decl element (`Document.charset(Charset)` → `ensureMetaCharsetElement` logic `src/main/java/org/jsoup/nodes/Document.java:268-269`, `301-317`).
